_readme: All heroines, their play styles, outfit layers and story. Edit freely: the game reads this file at start. Stats: speed = paddle top speed (px/s), size = paddle radius (px), reaction = seconds she sees the puck late (higher is easier), aim = how far her aim wanders (px), bank = 0..1 how often she banks shots, aggression = 0..1 how far forward she plays. Layer effects: speed/size multiply, reaction adds. attitude = what she thinks of you after N wins (0..6). Each match has a 'level': you need that level to play it (story wins earn most of it; pickup games and cups the rest). unlock_wins = story wins needed to meet her; unlock_done = heroines you must win over first. barks = lines she says during a match: 'hostile' for her first two matches, 'warm' after. finale = the championship gauntlet after all four are won over. Every character is an adult.

prologue.text: The Afterglow is an arcade lounge that stays open till three, and since last month it belongs to a bar chain. Tonight the chain's new night manager walks in for the first time.
That's you. Your first memo from head office says to shut down the regulars' after-hours game.
Oh, you're the suit? Great, cool, you towed my bike this morning, by the way, thanks for that.
It was in the fire lane.
You also got the job I've been doing unpaid for two years. Everyone hates you, if that helps you settle in.
Okay so the Last Call League has rules, everyone on the whiteboard signed them, it's first to five, and if you score a power smash the other player loses a layer.
Beat us at our own game and maybe the league lets you stay. Lose, and you write head office a letter saying you quit.

Every win changes what they think of you and unlocks a scene. Across the street, the owner of the Static has heard about league night, and Sable, who founded the Afterglow, has started showing up to watch.

mila.name: Mila Reyes
mila.tagline: Bike courier. Plays fast, talks faster. You towed her bike.
mila.grudge: You towed her bike on your first morning.
mila.signature_tip: A dead-straight rocket at the middle of your goal. Park your paddle in the centre of the mouth when you see the warning.
mila.perk_text: Win Mila over to learn her Bullet: your smash flies straight at the middle of her goal.

her_goal: Ha! Go back to your spreadsheet.
hostile.strip1: Oh you did not just do that. Fine, fine, I'm still faster.
hostile.strip2: Stop staring and play, you creep!
hostile.strip3: Nope, no, this isn't happening, I refuse.

your_goal: Do that again. No, wait, don't.
warm.strip1: You've been waiting all night for that one, huh?
warm.strip2: Eyes on the puck. Or on me, I guess, your call.
warm.strip3: Okay, you win this round. Mostly.

before.text: Twenty-eight bucks to get my bike out of the impound. I'm taking it out of your dignity.
I'll pay you back if you win.
Oh, I'm winning. And then you're writing that letter.

after.text: No. No way. Best of three!
League rules say one match a night.
Then I'll be back tomorrow. Don't you dare tow anything.

choice.text: Bring cash next time. The impound's twenty-eight.

reply.text: You are the worst person I've ever met. See you tomorrow.

choice.text: Here's your twenty-eight bucks. Keep the bike out of the fire lane.

reply.text: You're paying me back even though you won? That's so annoying.

choice.text: Same time tomorrow? It's a date.

reply.text: It is NOT a date. It's a rematch. Wear something easier to beat.

scene.title: Sore Loser
scene.brief: Mila sits on the edge of the table in whatever she has left, arms crossed, glaring at you and refusing to admit she's blushing.

before.text: I brought exact change for the impound this time. Out of spite.
I spent your twenty-eight bucks on new brake pads. Thanks. Don't make it weird.
For the record, this is not a date.
I watched my own replays all day and it turns out I lean left when I panic, so tonight I'm leaning right, or straight, or whatever, just not left.
Also I wore an extra layer. Strategy.
Huh, that's actually smart.
Don't compliment me, it's weird.

after.text: I leaned left. I leaned so far left.
You're not totally awful, for a suit. Walk me to my bike? I'm not exactly dressed for the street.

choice.text: Want me to call you a tow truck?

reply.text: Touch my bike and die. ...Okay, that was a little funny.

choice.text: Take my jacket. It's cold out.

reply.text: It smells like printer toner and something nice. Shut up.

choice.text: I'd walk you anywhere dressed like that.

reply.text: Eyes up, suit. ...Okay, eyes wherever.

scene.title: Borrowed Jacket
scene.brief: Outside under the neon sign, Mila wears your work jacket and nothing much under it, leaning on her bike, still pretending to be annoyed.

before.text: I parked three blocks away so you can't tow it. I'm a genius.
I still have your jacket. I'm keeping it. It's a courier thing.
I told Dex you checked me out. He made a second sign.
I brought backup. Every courier in the city is watching tonight.
Six couriers in rain gear crowd the bar, chanting her name and booing yours.
Dex turned the table's air all the way up. Couriers' rules: the puck never stops, and neither do we.
Is that a sign with my face crossed out?
Dex made it, he's really proud of it, so don't embarrass me in front of my people.

after.text: The couriers go quiet. Then Dex starts a slow clap, and the whole crew joins in.
Traitors, every one of them. Now they're asking if you're single.
I told them you're terrible. Hands off.

choice.text: Tell them I'm taken. By the bar chain.

reply.text: Ugh. Fine. I'll tell them you're married to a spreadsheet.

choice.text: Tell Dex the sign was great.

reply.text: He's going to frame that. You've made a friend for life. Gross.

choice.text: Tell them I'm single. Tell them first.

reply.text: You can tell them yourself. Or not. Whatever. Don't.

scene.title: Courier Crowd
scene.brief: Mila in her crop top and bike shorts stands on the table rail, pointing at you in mock outrage while her courier friends cheer offscreen. She's fighting a grin.

before.text: The couriers say hi to your spreadsheet.
Dex framed your compliment. It's in the depot next to the first aid kit.
I didn't tell anyone you're single. Just so you know. Nobody.
Mila comes in out of the pouring rain, soaked through, wheeling her bike on a flat back tyre.
Not one word about the hair.
I have a patch kit in the office.
Why do you have a patch kit?
I bought one after the towing thing, just in case.
That's either really sweet or really creepy. Play me while I decide.
Also Juno keeps asking me what you're like after close. I said loud and bad at darts. She didn't believe me.

after.text: You patched it while I was changing, didn't you? It's fixed.
Okay, sweet, I'm going with sweet.
Stay till the rain stops? I'm not riding home like this, and the towel only covers so much.

choice.text: Only if you admit the hair looks great wet.

reply.text: It looks GREAT wet and you know it.

choice.text: I'll make tea. Stay as long as you like.

reply.text: Tea. Okay. You're sweet, it's disgusting. Two sugars.

choice.text: The towel's doing a terrible job. I'm not complaining.

reply.text: Come closer and say that.

scene.title: Rain Check
scene.brief: Mila sits on the bar wrapped in a lounge towel, hair dripping, watching you patch her bike tyre on the floor. Her wet clothes hang off a bar stool.

before.text: My hair's dry, before you start.
I bought the same box of your terrible office tea. Don't read into it.
I've been thinking about the towel thing. A lot. Rack the puck.
Race rules tonight. Two minutes on Dex's phone timer, and whoever's ahead when it beeps wins. Couriers settle everything with a clock.
And if it's a tie?
Next goal wins. Sudden death. My favourite kind.
Dex keeps asking when you're coming to courier trivia night. I keep telling him never.
Mostly because I want you to myself. Forget I said that, rack the puck.

after.text: Okay, I give up pretending I'm still mad at you. It's exhausting.
Buy me fries, the big ones, since we're apparently whatever this is now.

choice.text: Small fries. You lost the right to large.

reply.text: I WON. Wait, no, I didn't. Okay, medium.

choice.text: Large fries, extra sauce, and a ride home.

reply.text: You're doing it again, the sweet thing. Never stop.

choice.text: Fries, then breakfast, then whatever this is.

reply.text: Whatever this is sounds really good.

scene.title: Fries at 4 AM
scene.brief: Mila in her sports bra and your jacket, sharing fries with you on the lounge's back steps at dawn, leaning on your shoulder.

alt_scene.title: Sunrise Ride
alt_scene.brief: Dawn on the empty boulevard: Mila in your work jacket over her sports bra and bike shorts rides no-hands circles around you, laughing, as the Afterglow sign switches off behind her.

before.text: Medium fries. You owe me a large, by the way. With interest.
You drove me home and didn't even try anything. I was almost offended.
So. Whatever this is. Tonight we find out.
Last race. Full air, two minutes on the clock, everything on the line.
No jokes tonight. If I win, you buy breakfast for a week.
And if I win?
Then I stop pretending I keep coming back for the hockey.

after.text: Fine, you win, I like you, there, I said it, can we eat now?
Here, have my Bullet. I'll teach you the wrist thing later, because the blinds are down and you owe me a different kind of rematch.

choice.text: Took you long enough.

reply.text: Shut up and kiss me.

choice.text: I like you too. Since the impound receipt.

reply.text: That's the dumbest, best thing anyone's ever said to me.

choice.text: Say it again. Slower.

reply.text: I. Like. You. Now lock the door.

scene.title: After Hours
scene.brief: Mila's romance scene in the closed lounge. Adult scene: write to your content plan.

juno.name: Juno Hart
juno.tagline: Bartender. Never hits the puck straight. You took her job.
juno.grudge: You got the manager job she'd been doing for free.
juno.signature_tip: A wall shot that loses no speed on the bounce. Watch which wall she aims at and meet it on the rebound.
juno.perk_text: Win Juno over to learn her Ricochet: your smash banks off the far wall without losing speed.

hostile.strip1: It's a vest. I have plenty of dignity left.
hostile.strip2: If you say one word, I'm spitting in your drinks forever.
hostile.strip3: Congratulations. You're the worst person I know.

warm.strip1: Mm. That one I let you have.
warm.strip2: You're blushing more than I am. Focus.

before.text: I ran this place for two years, right down to fixing the claw machine, and then they sent a stranger with a lanyard.
I didn't ask for the job.
Then losing it shouldn't hurt. Straight shots are for people who can't do geometry.

after.text: You read the wall. Nobody reads the wall.
This changes nothing. You're still a lanyard.

choice.text: Nice lanyard insult. Got any others?

reply.text: Forty-one. I wrote them down.

choice.text: You run this place better than I ever will.

reply.text: Don't. I'm busy hating you.

choice.text: Teach me the wall thing sometime?

reply.text: Sure. Private lessons cost extra. Your dignity.

scene.title: Behind the Bar
scene.brief: Juno, half out of her uniform, slams a drink down in front of you, furious, and refuses to admit she lost.

before.text: Lanyard insult number two: clipboard with legs.
I've been thinking about what you said. I hate that I've been thinking about it.
Lesson one: the wall is your friend. I am not. Rack 'em.
I've drawn every angle on this table on a napkin. Forty-one napkins.
Is that why we're out of napkins?
Don't be charming. It doesn't suit you.
House rules tonight: bank shots count double. Straight shots are a waste of a perfectly good wall.

after.text: Forty-two napkins, and none of them had you on it.
I read your memo. You never sent the order to shut us down. Why not?
Because this place is the only thing that chain bought that's worth anything.

choice.text: Also, I needed your napkins for my list of comebacks.

reply.text: Steal my napkins, steal my heart. Wait, no. Forget I said that.

choice.text: This place is yours. I just have the badge.

reply.text: Stop being nice. I can't think straight when you're nice.

choice.text: Maybe I wanted an excuse to keep seeing you.

reply.text: That's a terrible excuse. Keep using it.

scene.title: The Memo
scene.brief: Juno in her slip on the office desk, reading your unsent memo by lamplight, looking up at you differently for the first time.

before.text: I counted the napkins again. You owe me three.
I put your name on the staff rota. As a joke. Mostly.
Still using that excuse? Good.
Inventory night. You count bottles, I count your mistakes.
Why is there a case of maraschino cherries marked 'emergency'?
Because some nights are emergencies. Rack 'em, loser counts the limes.

after.text: You kept my schedule. Not one shift moved.
It was a good schedule.
Nobody has ever said that to me. I need a minute, and the emergency cherries.

choice.text: Save me a cherry. I count those too.

reply.text: You get one. Emergency rations.

choice.text: It's your schedule. It always was.

reply.text: If you keep saying things like that I'm going to cry on the limes.

choice.text: I'd keep your schedule forever.

reply.text: Careful. I might hold you to that.

after.text: On her way out, Juno stops at the office printer. There's a page in the tray from head office: a plan to 'replace legacy bar staff', with your name in the approval box.
You smiled at me all night with this sitting in the printer?
Juno, wait, read the...
Save it, lanyard.

scene.title: Stockroom
scene.brief: Juno in her silk shirt, half buttoned with the sleeves rolled up, sits on a stack of beer crates in the stockroom with a clipboard and a pen between her teeth, eating cherries from the jar.

before.text: Rematch. I loosened the felt on your paddle, so tonight you're playing with about four fifths of one. Call it severance.
That's sabotage.
That's geometry. Smaller paddle, worse angles. Rack the puck.
And no, you don't get a cherry.
'It's your schedule,' you said. And then I found that page.
'Forever,' you said. Funny word.

after.text: Halfway through, an auditor from head office walks in. You show him round the lounge with Juno's wobbly paddle still in your hand.
You told him I built the stock system, the rota and the cocktail list.
You did.
You could have taken the credit. That's what lanyards do.
And that printout was the plan I refused to sign. You stopped at page one. Page two is where I wrote 'over my dead body' in the margin.
I sabotaged a paddle over a page I didn't finish reading.
I'm so mad I could kiss you. So I might.

choice.text: You owe me a paddle.

reply.text: I'll buy you ten. I'll name them all after you.

choice.text: You should have read page two. But I get it.

reply.text: You get it. Of course you get it. Ugh. Come here.

choice.text: So kiss me.

reply.text: Office. Now. Bring the champagne.

after.text: I stole the good champagne from the auditor's welcome basket.
Office, come on. We're celebrating you being a decent human being, which in this business is rare.

scene.title: Credit Where Due
scene.brief: Juno in her slip and your blazer lounges on the office couch, popping a stolen bottle of champagne, laughing as the cork hits the ceiling.

before.text: Paddle number one is called Lanyard. It lives in the office.
I read everything to the last page now. Even menus.
About the office the other night. I'm not sorry.
Proposal. You keep the title, I keep running the place, and we both lie to head office.
Deal. Winner picks who does payroll.
Mila's been ordering fries here every night and staring at the office door. Subtle, that one.

after.text: Fine, I'll do payroll. You'd mess it up anyway.
Stay for a nightcap. I'll make the one that isn't on the menu.

choice.text: Is it strong enough to make me forget payroll?

reply.text: It's strong enough to make you forget your name.

choice.text: Make two. One for the best manager this place ever had.

reply.text: That's you now. Shut up. Drink.

choice.text: Only if you drink it with me.

reply.text: That was always the plan.

scene.title: Off the Menu
scene.brief: Juno sits on the bar in her underwear and your tie, sliding you a glowing cocktail with a small smile.

alt_scene.title: Napkin Math
alt_scene.brief: Juno in her slip and reading glasses sits on the bar, scribbling shot angles on a napkin pressed flat against your chest, smirking like she's already won.

before.text: I'm still doing payroll. You're still bad at it.
You called me the best manager this place ever had. I wrote it on a napkin.
Same cocktail tonight? I'm making two.
Bank night, one last time. Every wall counts double, like it always should have.
Last napkin. It just says: don't fall for the new guy.
So I'd better win, huh?

after.text: I'm keeping that napkin. Framing it, actually.
Here's my Ricochet. The trick is to aim at the wall like you mean it. Now lock the door, manager.

choice.text: Frame it next to the forty-one insults.

reply.text: Right in the middle of them.

choice.text: Hang it behind the bar where everyone can see.

reply.text: Everyone. Okay. Yeah. I'd like that.

choice.text: Write a new one: fell for the new guy anyway.

reply.text: Already did. Lock the door.

scene.title: Perfect Angle
scene.brief: Juno's romance scene behind the bar. Adult scene: write to your content plan.

kat.name: Kat Vance
kat.tagline: Owns the Static, the dive bar across the street. Your league night stole her crowd.
kat.grudge: Your chain's league night flyers stole her Thursday crowd, and one ended up taped to her door.
kat.signature_tip: Leaves slow and keeps speeding up. Step up and meet it before the centre line, while it's still slow.
kat.perk_text: Win Kat over to learn her Slingshot: your power shot leaves slow and speeds up all the way to her goal.

her_goal: Slow start, big finish. Like me.
hostile.strip1: That's one jacket, I've got nine of them, so keep dreaming.
hostile.strip2: My band's on this shirt! Show some respect!
hostile.strip3: This never happened, and nobody across the street hears about it.

her_goal: That one had extra spin, just for you.
warm.strip1: You'd better be planning to give that jacket back.
warm.strip2: Like the band? I'll play you the record. Later.
warm.strip3: Eyes up here, champ. Eh, I'll allow it.
warm.signature: Wait for it... wait for it...

before.text: A woman in a leather jacket slams the door open and slaps a crumpled flyer on the bar.
'League night at the Afterglow, every Thursday.' Somebody taped this to my door. Thursday's been my night since before you could drink.
Head office did the flyers, I just work here.
Kat Vance, I own the Static, and my regulars are drinking here now, so guess what, I'm joining your stupid league.
If I win, the flyers stop. If you win, well, you won't.

after.text: That table's tilted. That's the only explanation.
It's not tilted. I level it every Monday.
Then I'll be back next Thursday, and every Thursday after that until it tilts my way.

choice.text: Juno levels it every Monday. I watched her.

reply.text: Then Juno's in on it.

choice.text: Sorry about the flyer. Really.

reply.text: Sorry doesn't pay my rent. ...But thanks.

choice.text: Come back Thursday. I'll save you a seat.

reply.text: I don't need a seat. I need a rematch.

scene.title: Wrong Bar
scene.brief: Kat stands at the table in her band tee and jeans, leather jacket thrown on the floor, jabbing a finger at you, furious and flushed.

before.text: I checked. Juno is not in on it. She is terrifying, though.
You apologised. Nobody from your chain ever apologises. It's thrown me off.
Nobody saved me a seat. I checked.
I've been practising on the Static's table. It's older than you and it has a dead spot in the corner.
If I can beat that table, you're nothing.
Why not just get a new table?
With what money? Somebody stole my Thursdays.
She drags you across the street to play on the Static's table, which has two steel bumpers bolted to the centre line.
My uncle put those in in 1994 and nobody's been able to get them off since. Home table advantage.

after.text: Fine, it's not the table, you're just annoyingly good.
What if the Static hosted league night on Mondays? We're closed Mondays.
You'd send people to my bar? Why?
Because the league's better with two bars.

choice.text: Also, your table is a crime.

reply.text: My table is a legend.

choice.text: The Static deserves a crowd.

reply.text: Yeah. It does. Okay. Mondays.

choice.text: And I'd get to see you every Monday.

reply.text: You're doing that thing. Stop. Keep going.

scene.title: Dead Spot
scene.brief: Kat in her band tee and ripped jeans sits on the bar of the empty Static across the street, its old table behind her, arms folded, studying you suspiciously.

before.text: My legendary table would like an apology.
I printed new flyers. Real ones, with my bar on them.
It's Monday. You're here. I noticed.
The Static's first league night is a Monday, and the place is packed. Kat looks terrified.
There are forty people in my bar. I haven't had forty people in my bar since the Super Bowl.
I widened the goals for tonight. Crowds like scoring. Don't argue, it's my bar.
Play me first and make it look good. If I lose in front of them I'll still kill you.

after.text: They're buying drinks. So many drinks.
You did this and I hate how much I love it. Shut up and have a beer.

choice.text: You owe me a percentage.

reply.text: Of what? Okay, fine, free beer for life.

choice.text: This is all you. I just sent the flyer.

reply.text: Stop deflecting. I'm hugging you.

choice.text: Have a beer with me after close.

reply.text: After close, then. Don't be late.

scene.title: Monday Night
scene.brief: Kat behind the bar of the packed Static in her band tee and jeans, pulling two pints at once and laughing, the crowd a neon blur behind her.

before.text: Free beer for life starts tonight. One per night. Don't push it.
I still owe you a hug. Two hugs. I'm counting.
After close last time was nice. Nicer than nice.
Sable came to my Monday night. Sat at the bar, ordered a gin, told me my bass was flat. Best night of my life.
I got my band back together for the Static's Monday nights. We play after league.
Our drummer quit. So, unrelated question: can you keep a beat?
Is that a job offer?
It's a dare. Beat me first.
We're playing on the stage table during soundcheck. House lights stay off, so all you get is the stage lights. Good luck.

after.text: You can't drum, which is fine, nobody can.
Stay for soundcheck anyway. I want someone to watch who isn't Juno judging my bass.

choice.text: I was a natural on drums.

reply.text: You were a disaster on drums. Stay anyway.

choice.text: You sounded amazing.

reply.text: You're just saying that. Say it again.

choice.text: I'd watch you play all night.

reply.text: Careful. I play long sets.

scene.title: Soundcheck
scene.brief: Kat on the Static's tiny stage in a cropped band tee and jeans, bass guitar slung low, grinning at you over the mic stand under red stage lights.

before.text: Our drummer heard about your audition. He came back. Out of fear.
I played better knowing you were listening. That's a stupid thing to say.
Long set tonight. Hope you're ready.
So I found out head office taped that flyer to my door. Not you.
You took the blame for two months and never said a word.
You needed someone to be mad at.
That's the most annoying nice thing anybody's done for me. Play me before I cry.

after.text: I tore up the flyer but kept the bit with your chain's logo on it, for darts.
Walk me home? I know it's across the street. Walk slow.

choice.text: It's forty feet, Kat.

reply.text: Then walk really, really slow.

choice.text: I'd walk you across town.

reply.text: Across the street is plenty. For now.

choice.text: I'll walk you home, and up the stairs.

reply.text: Upstairs comes later. Keep walking.

scene.title: Across the Street
scene.brief: Kat in her band tee and your work jacket stands in the middle of the empty street between the two bars at 4 AM, both neon signs glowing behind her, reaching for your hand.

alt_scene.title: Encore
alt_scene.brief: After close at the Static, Kat in a cropped tee and your work jacket stands on the little stage with her bass, pulling you up by your tie under red stage lights.

before.text: Forty feet took us twenty minutes. New record.
For now, I said. It's later now.
You remembered the stairs. Good.
Two games tonight, one in each bar. Win both, or it doesn't count.
No trash talk tonight. Every sentence I start comes out nice and it's horrible.
Okay, bet. I win, you play bass in my band forever. You win, and...
I win?
You win, you find out what the Static's upstairs apartment looks like.

after.text: Okay, you win. Upstairs, and mind the steps, they're older than the table.
Take my Slingshot too. Start slow, finish strong, like tonight.

choice.text: Your stairs are a deathtrap.

reply.text: Then hold on to me.

choice.text: Thank you for letting me in.

reply.text: Thank you for taking the blame. And everything after.

choice.text: Show me the apartment. Slowly.

reply.text: Slowly. Got it.

scene.title: Upstairs at the Static
scene.brief: Kat's romance scene in her apartment above the Static. Adult scene: write to your content plan.

before.text: One game down. Kat grabs your hand and walks you across the street to the Static for the second.
Best of two bars. Mine has the bumpers, so this is where the real match is.

sable.name: Sable Marchetti
sable.tagline: Founded the Afterglow, sold it to your chain. Undefeated for six years.
sable.grudge: You're the face of the company that bought her lounge.
sable.signature_tip: Leaves wide and curls back into your goal. Don't chase where it starts; cover where it bends to.
sable.perk_text: Win Sable over to learn her Hook: your smash curls into the goal from a wide angle.
sable.unlock: Win over two of the others (all 6 of their matches)

her_goal: Is that all the company sent?
your_goal: Enjoy it while it lasts, darling.
hostile.strip1: Nobody has seen me without this blazer in six years. Enjoy the view, because it will not happen twice.
hostile.strip2: You are starting to annoy me.
hostile.strip3: Well played. I do not enjoy saying that.

warm.strip1: Go on, then. You have earned a look.
warm.strip2: You have made me nervous. I will be sending you the bill.
warm.strip3: I do not lose. I allowed you tonight, which is different.
warm.signature: Can you read the curve yet?

before.text: I built this place with my own hands and sold it to keep the lights on, and now they have sent you to tidy up what is left.
My regulars like you now. I do not, so show me why I should.

after.text: Six years, and nobody had seen what is under this blazer.
Do not get comfortable. That was a warm-up.

choice.text: Warm-up? You were sweating.

reply.text: Women do not sweat. We glow. Furiously.

choice.text: You built something special here.

reply.text: I know. That is what makes this so painful.

choice.text: I'd like to see what's under the next layer.

reply.text: Earn it.

scene.title: Under the Blazer
scene.brief: Sable leans back on the table, blazer gone, eyes narrowed, studying you like a problem she plans to destroy.

before.text: I have been glowing furiously all week.
You said I built something special. I keep hearing it.
You wanted to earn it. So earn it.
I closed early tonight, so there is no audience.
Whatever happens on this table stays between us and the security camera I just unplugged.
I set the terms tonight. Pick your poison.

choice.text: Mini goals

reply.text: Precision, then. Good, you will need it.

choice.text: By the Book: no power shots

reply.text: No smashes, no tricks. Just you and the angles.

after.text: My hands are shaking. That has not happened since my first tournament.
Juno told me about the memo you never sent. Come upstairs, we should talk.

choice.text: Bringing the security camera?

reply.text: I unplugged it. Do keep up.

choice.text: Whatever you need to say, I'm listening.

reply.text: That is a rare quality in a man with a lanyard.

choice.text: Lead the way.

reply.text: I always do.

scene.title: The Office
scene.brief: Sable in her old office in stockings and little else, lit pink by the neon sign through the window, pouring two drinks.

before.text: The camera is still unplugged, in case you wondered.
You listened, last time. I am not used to that.
You followed me upstairs very obediently last week.
I found the box from opening night, nine years ago. The first menu is in there, with the photos and the original sign.
Win, and I'll show you. Lose, and it goes back in the closet with my feelings.
New terms. Choose quickly, I do not like to wait.

choice.text: Rush Clock

reply.text: Two minutes. I have won entire tournaments in less.

choice.text: Play with a smaller paddle

reply.text: Bold. Or foolish. We will find out which.

after.text: That is me at twenty-two, with a borrowed table and a terrible haircut.
I never wanted to sell. I would like someone to know that, and I suppose it is you.
Then let's get it back.

choice.text: Nice haircut, by the way.

reply.text: I will have you killed.

choice.text: Twenty-two-year-old you would be proud.

reply.text: Twenty-two-year-old me would have told you to get lost. Thirty-one-year-old me is thinking about it.

choice.text: You were cute then. You're dangerous now.

reply.text: Correct on both counts.

scene.title: Opening Night
scene.brief: Sable in her corset top sits on her office floor surrounded by old photos of the Afterglow's opening night, laughing at one of them, eyes a little wet.

before.text: I burned the haircut photo. Do not ask.
I framed the first menu. It is on my desk, facing your chair.
Dangerous, you said. Let us see how dangerous.
Kat Vance tells me you play bass now. Badly. She sounded proud.
Head office wants to turn the Afterglow into a sports bar with big screens, wings and no table.
Over my dead lanyard.
Good answer. Now show me you will fight for it.
Tonight's terms are about trust. Pick one.

choice.text: Blackout

reply.text: In the dark, then. You will have to feel where the puck is.

choice.text: Turbo Air

reply.text: Fast, then. Try to keep up.

after.text: You fight dirty. I like that in a co-conspirator.
Come up to the roof. I think better up there, and I am not putting the corset back on.

choice.text: A candy cigarette? Very tough.

reply.text: It is grape. Show some respect.

choice.text: I'll fight for this place with you. Whatever it takes.

reply.text: Whatever it takes. I will hold you to that.

choice.text: Lead me anywhere.

reply.text: Roof first. Then we will see.

scene.title: Rooftop
scene.brief: Sable in stockings and your dress shirt sits on the roof ledge beside the buzzing neon sign, city lights behind her, holding a candy cigarette like a real one.

before.text: I bought more grape candy cigarettes. Do not judge me.
Whatever it takes, you said. It is going to take a lot.
The roof was a good start.
I have decided to buy the Afterglow back, with your help. Every good plan needs a spy inside head office.
But I do not partner with people I can beat. Prove it again.
Partners negotiate. You choose my handicap for once.

choice.text: Bank Night for you

reply.text: Your banks count double. Generous of me, I know.

choice.text: Wide goals for both of us

reply.text: Big goals, big scores, big risks. I approve.

after.text: Partners, then, fifty-fifty. You may even keep the lanyard.
Head office will sell if we can prove this place makes money, so we give them one enormous night: the Last Call Championship.
Partners celebrate. Stay a while.

choice.text: Fifty-fifty? I want fifty-one.

reply.text: Then you will have to beat me for it, every night, forever.

choice.text: I'd partner with you on anything.

reply.text: Careful. I make long-term plans.

choice.text: How do partners celebrate?

reply.text: Close the door and find out.

scene.title: Partners
scene.brief: Sable in lingerie sits on the edge of her desk signing a napkin contract, pulling you in by your tie.

alt_scene.title: Hostile Takeover
alt_scene.brief: Sable in a tailored vest and open blazer sits in your office chair with her heels up on your desk, pointing a fountain pen at you like a weapon.

before.text: Fifty-one percent, you said. Tonight decides it.
Long-term plans. I drew one up. It has you in it.
Partners. I liked how we celebrated.
No terms tonight. No handicaps, no tricks. Just the two of us and the table, the way it started.
For the title. Winner's name goes at the top of the wall.
And me, win or lose, if I am honest. Do not tell the others I said that.

after.text: New champion. Your name goes on the wall tomorrow.
The Hook is yours. Tonight, though, you are mine. Champion's privilege works both ways.

choice.text: Champion's privilege. Got a list?

reply.text: Several. Alphabetical.

choice.text: My name goes up next to yours.

reply.text: Next to mine. Yes. That is where it belongs.

choice.text: Then take it.

reply.text: Oh, I intend to.

scene.title: Champion's Privilege
scene.brief: Sable's romance scene on the lounge's championship table. Adult scene: write to your content plan.

before.text: Championship night. Head office agreed: if the Afterglow sells out tonight, Sable can buy it back.
Every ticket's gone, and the Static's sold out too. Kat's got a screen up over there.
There's a line round the block, so I made a cocktail called The Lanyard. Gin and regret, mostly.
There are couriers on the roof and couriers on the bar, and Dex brought a drum!
League rules say the champion has to beat all four of us back to back, with no breaks.
In front of everyone?
In front of everyone. Last call, partner.
Me first! No mercy and no breakfast bets this time, just the Bullet.
I drew this match on a napkin and you lose on it. Prove the napkin wrong.
Half the Static's watching on the screen, so don't make me look bad. Or do, honestly, I'm past caring.
Six years undefeated until you. Let us see whether it was a fluke.

after.text: The bar goes up in a roar, someone sprays champagne over the crowd, and Dex puts a stick straight through his drum.
Head office signed the papers ten minutes ago. The Afterglow is ours.
Ours, as in I'm a co-owner now? I want that in writing, on a napkin.
Does this mean I get free fries forever?
The Static's officially the Afterglow's sister bar. We're making T-shirts.
Last call, everyone. Not you lot, you're staying.
The lounge empties out under the humming sign, and none of the five of you goes home.
